author: worker_1
belief: Benjamin Franklin served as an agent/spokesman for multiple American colonies (Pennsylvania, Georgia, New Jersey, Massachusetts) in Great Britain from 1757-1762 and 1764-1775. He was the leading spokesman for American interests in England, especially during the Stamp Act crisis in 1766 when he gave highly publicized testimony before the House of Commons.

author: worker_2
belief: Benjamin Franklin was highly regarded by his contemporaries: David Hume hailed him as America's "first great man of letters," Immanuel Kant called him "The Prometheus of Modern Times," he was called "the world's most famous American" for two decades before the Revolution, he was widely admired as U.S. ambassador to France, received the Royal Society's Copley Medal, and was celebrated in France with fashion trends, medallions, and engravings inspired by him.

author: worker_2
belief: Benjamin Franklin is highly regarded in historical assessments: ranked 6th in The Atlantic's 2006 survey of most influential Americans, 35th in Time Magazine's 2012 global ranking, called "the most accomplished American of his age and the most influential in inventing the type of society America would become," and is considered one of the leading Founding Fathers.
